RULES.topic: Absentee ballot receipt deadline — no postmark grace period
RULES.currentRule: Iowa eliminated the postmark-based grace period in its 2021 election-law overhaul. Absentee ballots are only valid if physically received by the county auditor by 8:00 PM on Election Day. A postmark before Election Day no longer extends the receipt deadline, except for (a) Safe at Home program participants whose ballots are received by the Secretary of State in time to transmit to the county auditor by noon the Monday after the election, and (b) UOCAVA (military/overseas) ballots received by noon the Monday after the election.
RULES.whyItMatters: IA-02 voters across all 22 counties must ensure their absentee ballot physically arrives at the county auditor's office by 8:00 PM on November 3, 2026 — mailing it on or near Election Day is risky. This is a stricter rule than many neighboring states that still honor a postmark grace period.
RULES.detail: See Franklin County's 2021 election-law summary and Adair County's mirrored page. NEEDS REVIEW: confirm exact statutory citation directly from Iowa Code/legislative text in a future pass.

RULES.topic: Absentee ballot-curing process for signature/affidavit defects
RULES.currentRule: If an absentee ballot's affidavit envelope is unsigned or otherwise defective, the county auditor must notify the voter in writing (and by phone/email if provided) within 24 hours of receipt. The voter may then: (1) request a replacement ballot and return it by 8:00 PM on Election Day; (2) vote in person at the polls on Election Day; or (3) sign/correct the affidavit in person at the county auditor's office by 8:00 PM on Election Day.
RULES.whyItMatters: IA-02 voters whose absentee ballot envelope is flagged for a signature or affidavit problem have a narrow but workable path to cure it before 8:00 PM on Election Day. Uniform statewide rule, not IA-02-specific.
RULES.detail: Iowa Administrative Code 721-21.355 (Notice to voter). Confirmed in plain language by Franklin County's election-law summary and Marion County Auditor FAQ.

RULES.topic: Voter ID requirements at the polls
RULES.currentRule: Iowa requires ID to cast a ballot. Acceptable primary forms: Iowa driver's license, Iowa non-operator's ID card, U.S. passport, U.S. military/veteran ID, a signed Iowa Voter ID card, or a tribal ID card/document. The Secretary of State issues free Voter ID cards to registered voters lacking another qualifying ID.
RULES.whyItMatters: IA-02 voters without one of the accepted forms of ID must obtain a free Iowa Voter ID card in advance or use a provisional ballot process on Election Day.
RULES.detail: Iowa Code Sections 48A.7A, 48A.10A, 49.78, 49.81 per NCSL's Voter ID Laws tracker.

RULES.currentRule: HF 2501, signed into law and effective July 1, 2026, eliminates the option for another registered voter to attest to (vouch for) the identity of a voter who lacks accepted ID. It also expands the definition of "election day" for misconduct investigations and centralizes city/school election filings with county auditors.
RULES.whyItMatters: Effective before the November 3, 2026 general election, IA-02 voters who previously could have used a fellow registered voter's attestation in lieu of ID must now cast a provisional ballot and return with valid ID within the applicable cure window. Sources disagree on whether that cure window is three days or noon the following Monday.
RULES.detail: Signed by Gov. Kim Reynolds, announced May 3, 2026; effective July 1, 2026. NEEDS REVIEW: exact provisional-ballot cure deadline (three days per Iowa Public Radio's framing of HF 2501, versus the older 'noon the Monday following the election' rule) should be confirmed against the enrolled bill text at legis.iowa.gov before publishing voter-facing content.

RULES.currentRule: Governed by Iowa Code Section 49.81. A prospective voter whose registration status is not active/pending, or who cannot establish required ID/residency (and, as of July 1, 2026, can no longer use attestation), casts a provisional ballot. Under the pre-2026 rule, the voter must provide the necessary ID either at the polling place before it closes at 8:00 PM, or at the county auditor's office by noon the following Monday.
RULES.whyItMatters: IA-02 voters flagged for ID or registration issues at the polls should understand the provisional-ballot process and cure window to ensure their vote counts.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: whether HF 2501 changed this cure deadline (some 2026 coverage says 'three days,' which may supersede the older 'noon Monday' rule) has not been confirmed against the enrolled bill text.

RULES.currentRule: HF 928, effective July 1, 2025, standardizes recount procedures across precincts and tightens recount-eligibility thresholds to 0.15% margin or less for statewide/federal races (1% or 50 votes, whichever is less, for other races). Recount administration shifted to county commissioners of elections (auditors) under Secretary of State oversight.
RULES.whyItMatters: If the IA-02 general election is decided by a very narrow margin, this statute governs whether and how a recount is triggered and conducted.
RULES.detail: Signed by Gov. Reynolds June 2, 2025; fully operative for the 2026 cycle per research; no reported repeal, injunction, or amendment found.

RULES.topic: Statewide ban on ranked-choice voting and registration-time citizenship verification (HF 954)
RULES.currentRule: HF 954 bans ranked-choice/instant-runoff voting statewide (effective January 1, 2026) and strengthens citizenship verification at the time of voter registration rather than at time of voting.
RULES.whyItMatters: Confirms IA-02's Nov. 3, 2026 general election will use traditional plurality voting, not ranked-choice, and that citizenship checks now occur at registration.
RULES.detail: Signed by Gov. Reynolds June 2, 2025; effective dates July 1, 2025 and January 1, 2026 per LegiScan bill tracker. Fully operative for 2026 per research; no reported repeal, injunction, or amendment found.

RULES.topic: Absentee ballot drop box siting restriction
RULES.currentRule: Iowa does not maintain a statewide drop-box locator or requirement. Iowa law (2021 reforms) permits, but does not require, county auditors to provide drop boxes, and any drop box must be located on the grounds of or within the building where the county auditor conducts in-person absentee voting.
RULES.whyItMatters: Unlike some states, IA-02 voters cannot rely on a network of freestanding neighborhood drop boxes; any drop box option is tied to the county auditor's own office location. Voters should check with their specific county auditor (all 22 IA-02 counties) for availability.
RULES.detail: NEEDS REVIEW: this is a structural constraint on the res-ballot-box resource tile — no single IA-02-wide drop-box URL exists; see RESOURCES notes.

CONFLICTS.factInQuestion: The exact length of the provisional-ballot ID cure window under HF 2501 for voters who previously relied on attestation and now lack accepted photo ID.
CONFLICTS.sourceAClaim: Iowa Public Radio's April 16, 2026 report on HF 2501's passage frames the post-attestation cure window as "three days" for a voter to return with valid ID.
CONFLICTS.sourceBClaim: The pre-2026 statutory framework under Iowa Code Section 49.81 (as summarized by county auditor pages such as Franklin County's) describes the provisional-ballot ID cure deadline as "noon the Monday following the election."
CONFLICTS.whyItMatters: IA-02 voters who cast a provisional ballot on November 3, 2026 due to lacking ID need a single, correct cure deadline. Using the wrong one on voter-facing content could cause a validly-curable ballot to go uncured, or create confusion about how much time is available.
CONFLICTS.suggestedReviewAction: Pull HF 2501's enrolled bill text directly from legis.iowa.gov to determine whether it amended the Iowa Code 49.81 cure deadline, and update rule-ia-hf2501-attestation-eliminated and rule-ia-provisional-ballots accordingly before publishing voter-facing content.
